events.factual_description: Harvestworks and Roulette co-present Live Processing Paint and Sound on Wednesday, October 28, 2026 at Roulette in Brooklyn. Doors are at 7:00 PM and the performance begins at 8:00 PM. The presenters list $25 advance, $30 at the door, and $20 student/senior admission. During Heidi Howard's live painting, Liz Phillips will process aquatic recordings in real time using Mugic and light sensors, contact microphones, a theremin, synthesizers and custom electronics, translating brushstrokes and fish activity into an immersive water soundscape; Howard is credited with sensors and live painting. Six camera/screen feeds provide live video synthesis on Roulette's projection screen. The program is presented as part of Harvestworks' 50th-anniversary celebration and also includes an introduction by Interim Director Ivana Dama and a conversation with e-flux Performance Curator Sanna Almajedi. Roulette states that a free livestream will be available at 8:00 PM and archived.

en.why_it_matters: The interesting instrument here is the feedback loop itself. Howard's brushstrokes and sensor data become active material while Phillips reshapes aquatic recordings through contact microphones, theremin, light sensing, synthesizers and custom electronics. That makes the room a live system rather than a playback surface, and the Harvestworks anniversary gives the experiment a useful historical frame around five decades of artists treating technology as part of the composition.
en.trip_verdict: If a New York trip already falls around October 28, this is worth folding into the evening at Roulette. From the DMV, I would pair it with another strong reason to be in the city rather than build a dedicated trip around this one performance; the free livestream also preserves a good fallback if the geography does not work.

es.why_it_matters: El instrumento interesante aquí es el propio circuito de retroalimentación. Las pinceladas y los sensores de Howard se vuelven material activo mientras Phillips transforma grabaciones acuáticas con micrófonos de contacto, theremin, sensores de luz, sintetizadores y electrónica propia. La sala funciona así como un sistema vivo y no como una simple superficie de reproducción; el aniversario de Harvestworks además coloca el experimento dentro de una historia de cinco décadas de artistas usando la tecnología como parte de la composición.
es.trip_verdict: Si un viaje a Nueva York ya cae alrededor del 28 de octubre, vale incorporar esta noche en Roulette. Desde el DMV la combinaría con otra razón fuerte para estar en la ciudad, en vez de construir un viaje dedicado alrededor de una sola función; el livestream gratuito también deja una buena alternativa si la geografía no cuadra.
